Thanks for the clear checklist, Soojin. Quick technical scope notes (to help Nebula finalize the questionnaire):

Proposed minimal "in scope" items for their vendor review (recommended)
- Hosting mode: Hosted API (Redwood public) — covers multi-tenant serving runtime. If Nebula requires Dedicated, we'll note additional controls.
- Data inputs: request/response payloads sent to model endpoints. We do not persist full customer prompts in long-term storage unless configured for caching/analytics (default retention 24h).
- KV cache: only exists in memory per request path; not materialized to object storage by default.
- Logs & telemetry: request metadata (timestamps, model_id, latency, token counts) stored in encrypted logs; payload redaction available on request.
- Model artifacts: we do not onboard customer model weights; we serve from our curated model catalog unless customer brings private model under Redwood Private.
- Backups & snapshots: runtime state is not backed up as persistent PII-bearing artifacts. Checkpointing applies to orchestration state only.

Evidence we can provide immediately:
- SOC2 Type II report (control coverage summary)
- KMS rotation policy excerpt + key management vendor info
- Network diagram showing public-hosted flow + optional VPC/private deployment notes (I will draft and upload).

Open question for Chris / procurement:
- If Nebula requires data residency in AWS-us-east-1 only, will that push them to Dedicated / Private offering? That impacts procurement pricing.

I'll draft a 1-page systems boundary diagram and the evidence checklist by Jan 3 to hit Soojin's Jan 5 delivery.

— Vivek
